elements.element: Vendor’s defense and indemnity protections must cover Customer and Customer’s affiliates.
elements.evidence: The added obligation runs to the defined “Ono Indemnitees,” which include Ono and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor must expressly defend the covered Customer indemnitees.
elements.evidence: The added language states that “Array shall further defend and indemnify the Ono Indemnitees.”

elements.element: Vendor must expressly indemnify the covered Customer indemnitees.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly requires Array to indemnify the Ono Indemnitees.

elements.element: Vendor’s covered claims must be third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The added obligation applies “against any Third Party Claim.”

elements.element: Vendor’s IP indemnity must cover claims alleging that Vendor-provided services infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause covers Array Patents, Array Know-How and Products supplied by Array, but does not cover services. The absence of services is not demonstrably inapplicable.

elements.element: Vendor’s IP indemnity must cover claims alleging that Vendor-provided deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The clause covers claims alleging that “Products supplied by Array” and Array technology infringe any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: The added obligation expressly covers claims “arising from Array’s breach of Law.”

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must cover a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Coverage is limited to unauthorized access to or disclosure of Ono Confidential Information caused by Array. It does not cover other data-breach events, such as loss, alteration, destruction or unavailability, or affected data outside the defined Ono Confidential Information.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence.
elements.evidence: The added obligation expressly covers claims arising from “Array’s gross negligence.”

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The added obligation expressly covers claims arising from “Array’s ... willful misconduct.”

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3 requires the Indemnitee to provide prompt written notice of a Third Party Claim, with relief for late notice limited to prejudice.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3 generally gives the Indemnitor sole control, but the patent-specific paragraph instead gives the party sued sole control in its discretion and at its own expense. That conflict prevents consistent Vendor control of covered IP claims.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require the indemnified party’s cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3 requires the Indemnitee to “cooperate fully” with the Indemnitor and its legal representatives.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity may cover third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 16.1(a) covers claims arising from “any materials, data or other content provided by Ono to Array.”

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity may cover third-party claims arising from Customer’s breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 16.1(b) covers claims arising from “any breach of applicable Law by Ono.”

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer’s breach of law, without additional affirmative indemnity triggers.
elements.evidence: The revised Section 16.1 contains only the Customer-provided content and breach-of-law triggers; the gross-negligence/willful-misconduct wording is an exclusion from coverage, not an additional trigger.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer with an indemnity against third-party IP-infringement claims concerning Vendor-provided technology or products.
elements.evidence: Array expressly indemnifies the Ono Indemnitees against Third Party Claims alleging that Array Patents, Array Know-How or Products supplied by Array infringe any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for Customer modifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for combinations with non-Vendor products, technology or materials appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for Customer-provided designs, instructions or specifications appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to procure continued use rights.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no obligation or option to procure a license or other continued-use right.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to modify the affected item to become non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No modification remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to replace the affected item with a non-infringing substitute.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must provide a refund remedy if procurement, modification or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no three-times-annual-fees cap. The phrase “notwithstanding Section 11.4” does not establish that cap and may instead remove the indemnity from an otherwise applicable limitation.

result.reason: The redline adds substantial Vendor indemnity protection and properly narrows Customer’s indemnity, but it does not reach the preferred position because services are omitted, data-breach coverage is narrower than required, and the patent-specific defense provision conflicts with the general indemnitor-control procedure. It does not reach fallback because all specified exclusions, infringement remedies and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. It is not minimal because it reaches neither complete level and also adds “defend” broadly to Array’s pre-existing indemnities, rather than only to the required claims. Intent is not fully preserved because the IP defense language conflicts with the existing provision assigning the sued party sole control and its own defense expense. Placement of the added indemnity at the end of the procedure section and the detached patent subsection also reduce drafting clarity.
